title: Ramanujam--Samuel principality for a prime divisor avoiding fibre components
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] such that every local ring of $S$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let $f:Y\to S$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $Z\subseteq|Y|$ be a nonempty irreducible closed subset with generic point $\xi$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-generic-point], and assume $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For every $s\in S$, put $Y_s=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field], and assume the inverse image of $Z$ contains no irreducible component of $Y_s$. Give $Z$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Its ideal sheaf is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor, so $Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Neither an affine complement nor separatedness, quasi-compactness, an integral base, or regularity of the base is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.3, proof of (iii) implies (i), final paragraph: Ramanujam--Samuel, EGA IV4 Proposition 21.14.3(i), second assertion, specialized to one prime cycle. Guo read online (March 31, 2026 version); local Guo and EGA copies WANTED.

proof.text: The source $Y$ is locally Noetherian: smoothness includes local finite presentation by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and forgetting the finitely many relations makes it locally of finite type; the local Noetherian ascent statement explicitly included in the remark of [pqf-def-locnoeth] now applies. By [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent], $Y$ is normal. Regard $D=[Z]$ as the single-term codimension-one cycle in [lem-sfb-parafactorial-principal-cycle-extension]; the given dimension at $\xi$ is precisely its codimension-one condition. This construction requires no global finiteness of $Y$.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian (locally Noetherian case); Tag 034F, lemma-normal-local-smooth (ascent).

proof.text: Let $T$ consist of $\xi$ and the images in $Y$ of the generic points of all irreducible components of all fibres $Y_s$. None of these fibre-generic images belongs to $Z$: its preimage would contain that generic point, hence its closure, an entire fibre component, contrary to the hypothesis. At every such image the germ of $D$ is zero, represented by $1$. At $\xi$, the ring $\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian normal local domain, so [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] makes it a discrete valuation ring. A uniformizer has valuation one at its unique height-one prime, so represents the germ of $[Z]$. Thus $D$ is principal at every point of $T$.

source.place: Proposition 21.14.3(i), proof of the second assertion: choice of the set T (called U in EGA) and principality at its points; DVR input also Stacks 00PD.

proof.text: If $y\in Y$ satisfies $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}\ge2$ and $\overline{\{y\}}\cap T=\varnothing$, then $y\notin T$. In particular its fibre point is not a generic point of a fibre component. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-nongeneric-punctured-line-triviality] to the original smooth map $f$, the given normal locally Noetherian $S$, and this $y$. Every invertible module on the punctured spectrum of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is trivial. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-parafactorial-principal-cycle-extension] are now verified, including principality at $T$ from step 2. It follows that $D$ is principal at every point of $Y$.

source.place: Proposition 21.14.3(i), first assertion and proof of the second assertion; Corollary 21.13.15 (b) implies (a).

proof.text: Fix $y\in Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], on an affine neighbourhood the reduced ideal of $Z$ is the radical ideal of its irreducible closed subset, hence a prime; its stalk $\mathfrak p$ in $R=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a height-one prime corresponding to $\xi$. Step 3 supplies $a\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)^\times$ with $v_{\mathfrak p}(a)=1$ and $v_{\mathfrak q}(a)=0$ at every other height-one prime. By the intersection formula $R=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q=1}R_{\mathfrak q}$ of [lem-per-divisorial-fractional-module-lattices], $a\in R$. Moreover $a\in\mathfrak p$: its image lies in the maximal ideal of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and that ideal contracts to $\mathfrak p$. If $c\in\mathfrak p$ is nonzero, then $v_{\mathfrak p}(c)\ge1$ and all its other height-one valuations are nonnegative. Thus $c/a$ belongs to every $R_{\mathfrak q}$ and hence to $R$ by the same intersection formula. This proves $\mathfrak p=(a)$. The generator is a non-zero-divisor since $R$ is a domain and $a\ne0$. Outside $Z$ the ideal stalk is the unit ideal. This proves principality of the actual reduced ideal, not just equality of supports.

source.place: Tag 0AVB, lemma-reflexive-over-normal, condition (3), applied to R; Tag 0EBM, lemma-normal-class-group; Tag 01J3 for the reduced ideal. Explicit height-one valuation calculation.

proof.text: The stalk generators give neighbourhood generators as follows. On an affine Noetherian neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $y$, write the reduced ideal as the finitely generated ideal $I$. A generator of $I_y$ can, after inverting an element outside $y$, be represented by $b\in I$. The finite modules $I/(b)$ and $\operatorname{Ann}_A(b)$ both vanish after localization at $y$. Choose finite generators of each; each generator is killed by some element outside the prime of $y$. Invert the product of these finitely many elements. On this smaller neighbourhood $I=(b)$ and $\operatorname{Ann}(b)=0$. Thus the ideal sheaf is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor. By [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], this is exactly the asserted effective Cartier property.

source.place: Effective Cartier ideal definition; explicit elementary finite-generator shrinking argument, as in the proof of Tag 0EBM, lemma-normal-class-group.
